items.hed: The Texans estimated running back David Montgomery as a full participant on Monday's walkthrough report, putting him on track to return Thursday night against the Colts after a groin injury sidelined him the past four games, while fellow back Woody Marks sat out with a new concussion
items.insight: The team did not practice Monday but was required to file an injury report ahead of Thursday night's short-week game against Indianapolis at Reliant Stadium; Montgomery returned to practice last Thursday and was a full participant Friday before going inactive again Sunday, and was again estimated as a full participant Monday, according to a Houston beat report. The Texans also estimated linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (foot/illness) and Marks (concussion, suffered in Sunday's loss to Cleveland) as non-participants, while linebacker Jake Hummel (groin) was limited.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still.

items.hed: Houston faces Tuesday's 6 p.m. ET deadline to set its 40-man roster ahead of the Rule 5 Draft, with right-hander James Hicks — the 2025 Arizona Fall League Pitcher of the Year — among the Astros prospects on the roster bubble
items.insight: All 30 clubs must add Rule 5-eligible players to their 40-man rosters by Tuesday evening or risk losing them in the Rule 5 Draft at December's Winter Meetings in San Diego, according to MLB.com. Hicks, a 13th-round pick in 2023 out of South Carolina, followed his Fall League honor with a 5.14 ERA across 24 Double-A starts this year; MLB.com's prospect staff says he has some of the best feel and deception in Houston's system but lacks a pitch that grades better than average, leaving his 40-man status one of the system's notable bubble calls.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still (page hero shared across today's Texas desk; Astros are in their off-season).

items.hed: The Rockets' win streak ended Monday night in Miami, where the Heat snapped Houston's run with a 128-110 victory to win their own fifth straight, dropping the Rockets to 11-4 on the season
items.insight: The league's own game recap shows the Heat improving to 8-6 with their fifth consecutive win while the Rockets fell to 11-4, according to NBA.com. The loss ends the stretch in which Houston had beaten Washington, Golden State and Utah this month, and the Rockets now turn to their next matchup looking to start a fresh run.
